security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, homepage URLs, and relative documentation links. The confirmed issue is the Resend connector command that can create and schedule email broadcasts. No prompt-injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Keep dry-run as the default, require explicit user approval before --live, verify consent and suppression status, and avoid exposing credentials in prompts or logs.
Prefer package-scoped reference names or marketplace resolver links where possible to reduce path traversal ambiguity in automated review.
Label prompt examples as plain text and avoid command-like formatting unless the agent is expected to run a command.

content.value_statement: Lifecycle email programs often fail because triggers, cadence, and exits are unclear. This skill creates structured flow maps, governance rules, and SEND N scoring.
actual_capabilities: Maps triggers, timing, goals, branches, and exits for lifecycle email flows.
Designs welcome, abandoned-cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, re-engagement, and B2B outbound sequences.
Sets global send caps, quiet hours, fatigue guardrails, and sunset rules.
Scores the SEND N dimension with sub-item notes and the relevant goal weight.
Creates a handoff summary for email creative or quality audit workflows.
limitations: It does not write full subject lines, body copy, or calls to action for each email.
It does not compute final EQS or enforce unsubscribe veto checks.
It does not design closed-loop re-consent programs for defined lapsed cohorts.
Precise timing depends on user-provided platform, segment, trigger, and performance data.

use_cases.title: Plan a Welcome Program
use_cases.description: Turn a signup trigger into a sequenced onboarding flow with goals, exits, and cadence controls.

use_cases.title: Recover Cart Abandonment
use_cases.description: Design a cart recovery sequence with discount branches, purchase exits, send caps, and fatigue protection.

use_cases.title: Structure Outbound Nurture
use_cases.description: Build a multi-step B2B outbound sequence with reply exits, goal progression, and suppression safeguards.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Welcome Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a welcome flow for a new account signup. Audience: [audience]. Product: [product]. ESP: [ESP]. Include trigger, timing, branches, exits, cadence rules, and SEND N score.

prompt_templates.title: Build Cart Recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an abandoned-cart sequence for [store]. Use [number] steps, [timing preference], discount branch, exit-on-purchase, complaint guardrails, and a handoff summary.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Lifecycle Cadence
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my current lifecycle program from this export summary: [paste details]. Identify missing flows, set send caps, quiet hours, fatigue guardrails, and sunset rules.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Full Nurture Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete nurture architecture for [business model]. Include welcome, browse, post-purchase, re-engagement, B2B outbound if relevant, SEND N scoring, and handoffs to creative and quality audit skills.

output_examples.input: Welcome flow for a B2B SaaS trial signup.
output_examples.output: A five-step onboarding sequence with signup trigger, day 0 orientation, activation nudges, feature education, trial conversion branch, reply and unsubscribe exits, and a SEND N score.

output_examples.input: Abandoned-cart recovery for an ecommerce store.
output_examples.output: A three-step cart sequence with browse context, purchase exit, discount branch, send cap, quiet hours, complaint guardrail, and creative handoff notes.
A cadence governance plan with lower send caps, fatigue pause rules, light re-engagement touch, sunset threshold, and open-loop notes for missing consent data.

best_practices: Provide the lifecycle goal, trigger event, audience segment, and current cadence before requesting a flow.
Separate flow architecture from email copy so each step has a clear job before writing begins.
Review consent, suppression, unsubscribe, and complaint signals before activating any sequence.
anti_patterns: Do not enroll every subscriber into every flow without lifecycle-stage rules.
Do not add discounts or extra sends without clear exit conditions and complaint guardrails.
Do not treat estimated timing as measured performance data.

faq.question: Does this skill write each email?
faq.answer: No. It designs the flow structure, timing, branches, exits, cadence rules, and handoff notes for copywriting.

faq.question: Can it design abandoned-cart sequences?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan steps, timing, discount branches, purchase exits, fatigue rules, and handoff requirements.

faq.question: Does it handle consent checks?
faq.answer: It requires consent and suppression facts before activation, but the consent registry remains the source of truth.

faq.question: Can it score email quality?
faq.answer: It scores the SEND N dimension only. Final EQS and veto checks belong to the quality audit workflow.

faq.question: What inputs improve the result?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include ESP, flow type, segment, trigger event, current export summary, complaint rate, and unsubscribe signals.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible skill hosts.
